The pattern matches a DNS rollout where internal‑dns‑02 received a new zone file that omitted the record, and pods forward queries randomly to the two authoritative DNS servers, causing alternating failures.","likely_cause":"Partial zone‑file rollout to internal‑dns‑02 that omitted the auth database DNS record, leading to mismatched answers and intermittent NXDOMAIN responses via the random forward plugin.","confidence":"medium","claims":[{"text":"auth‑service‑01 logged NXDOMAIN errors for its database name on 2025‑04‑21","evidence_ids":["log:1487"],"quote":"ERROR auth-service-01.prod.internal new database connection failed: lookup of auth database name answered NXDOMAIN"},{"text":"Pods forward queries to the two DNS servers at random, so differing answers appear intermittently","evidence_ids":["RB-020#3"],"quote":"The `forward` plugin picks an upstream at random for each query it sends"},{"text":"A recent zone‑file rollout to internal‑dns‑02 omitted a required record, causing one server to answer NXDOMAIN","evidence_ids":["RB-020#13"],"quote":"new file was missing `inventory-db-01.prod.internal`"}],"next_checks":["Query the auth database name directly against both internal‑dns‑01 and internal‑dns‑02 (dig @10.0.0.53 and @10.0.0.54) to see which returns NXDOMAIN","Compare the SOA serial numbers on the two DNS servers to confirm they differ","Inspect the current zone files on internal‑dns‑01 and internal‑dns‑02 for the presence of the auth database record","Review the rollout logs to verify whether internal‑dns‑02 received a new zone file missing the record"]}
